summary: Across the 104 articles tracked this week, social sentiment carried the heaviest negative share of the three categories at roughly 27%, ahead of political at 22% and economic at just under 14%. That ordering is somewhat different from prior weeks, where fuel and price news typically drags economic sentiment down; this week economic coverage was cushioned by several genuinely positive developments; a diesel price cut of roughly Rs30-32 per litre after government talks with refineries, Google opening its first Pakistan office, and progress on the $2.5bn ML-1 railway financing all pulled the category toward neutral-to-positive even as petrol and diesel prices ticked up twice during the week. Social sentiment's negative tilt, by contrast, tracks a steady run of security and unrest stories: intelligence-based operations against militants in Balochistan and KP reported almost daily, a Karachi vendor shot dead in a targeted separatist attack, monsoon flood warnings for several major cities, and a detained lady health workers' protest broken up by police.

If the week had one dominant storyline, it was the standoff between the government and the judiciary over jailed PTI founder Imran Khan. It ran through nearly every day from August 17 onward: the Supreme Court ordered his transfer to Shifa International Hospital for a medical exam, the government filed a review petition calling the order discriminatory, the petition was returned by the court registrar over procedural defects, Khan was ultimately examined at PIMS rather than Shifa and declared medically fit before being returned to Adiala jail, and PTI then accused the government of defying the court outright, announcing both a contempt petition and a long march for September 27. Coverage of this saga stayed procedurally even-handed, generally presenting the government's stated rationale alongside PTI's objections, though a few individual dispatches (built around a single minister's or petitioner's remarks) were flagged with a pro-government or pro-opposition lean simply because no rebuttal was available within that particular article.

A second, quieter thread ran alongside it: pressure over fuel and provincial politics. Jamaat-i-Islami's petroleum-levy sit-in, which began the prior week, continued through Aug 16-17 with explicit warnings it could escalate into a broader anti-government movement, while a cited security-think-tank assessment reported Balochistan's conflict deaths up roughly 241% and security-personnel deaths up over 900% year-on-year, a sharp escalation sitting underneath the week's routine 'militants killed' operational announcements. Separately, the long-simmering proposal to redraw Pakistan's provincial map, splitting Punjab, Balochistan and KP and carving federal territory out of Sindh ahead of a proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment, resurfaced with MQM-P pushing for dialogue and Sindh's government warning the idea risks ethnic unrest. Parliament also passed defence-forces and National Command Authority amendment legislation over an opposition walkout, adding a fourth distinct source of institutional friction to a week already carrying several.

On confidence and framing: a large share of this week's flagged stories, especially from Business Recorder, were rated 'low' or 'medium' confidence because the outlet's article pages returned 403 errors, leaving Miqyas working only from RSS description excerpts rather than full text; that's a structural access issue rather than a reporting-quality one, but it means several of the week's more consequential claims (the Balochistan casualty statistics, the AJK reserved-seat schedule, Bilawal's withdrawal of legislative support) carry more uncertainty than usual. Political lean stayed 'balanced' on almost all flagged stories even through the Imran Khan standoff and the provinces debate, largely because Miqyas attributed contested claims to the party or official making them (PTI's accusations, the government's justifications, MQM-P's proposal, Sindh's rebuttal) rather than stating any of them as settled fact.

notableStories.headline: PTI slams govt for 'flouting' SC order, opp says it will approach SC over contempt
notableStories.context: The week's central storyline reached its sharpest point here: after the government examined Imran Khan at PIMS instead of the court-ordered Shifa Hospital, PTI accused it of defying the Supreme Court outright and announced both a contempt petition and a September 27 long march.

notableStories.headline: JI vows to continue sit-in until petroleum levy abolished
notableStories.context: Jamaat-i-Islami's open-ended sit-in against the petroleum levy, with an explicit warning it could escalate into a wider movement, captures the week's undercurrent of public strain over fuel and food prices.

notableStories.headline: Over 9 terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: state media
notableStories.context: Beyond the operation itself, the story cited independent security-assessment data showing Balochistan's overall conflict deaths up roughly 241% and security-personnel deaths up over 900% this year, a sharp deterioration behind the week's routine security bulletins.

notableStories.headline: New administrative units 'under serious consideration'
notableStories.context: Confirmation that the government is seriously weighing splitting Punjab, Balochistan and KP and carving federal territory out of Sindh, ahead of a proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment, a historically contentious idea most political parties currently oppose.

notableStories.headline: Defence forces, NCA amendment bills sail thru parliament
notableStories.context: Parliament passed legislation restructuring the armed forces' command structure and the National Command Authority framework over an opposition walkout, a distinct institutional flashpoint alongside the week's judiciary standoff and provincial-boundary debate.
